_comment: Cross-engine SCORECARD conformance. The Python core (app/logic.py evaluate_scorecard) is the source of truth; every `expected` block was produced by CALLING it, not by hand. Arms that consume this file MUST reproduce `expected.score` exactly for every case, and (where they implement the feature) the breakdown, woe_details, information_value and metrics. Scorecard shape is the Python/Kotlin/Dart shape (`bins` of factors with `ranges` and optional `woe_values`), NOT the TypeScript `factors`/`bands` shape in packages/rule-engine. evaluate_scorecard has no band/grade concept, so no case records one. `score` is always an integer, so it is an EXACT assertion; floats (woe, contribution, information_value, metric values) compare within meta.floatTolerance. A metric whose formula fails is recorded as {"error": true} because the real message embeds CPython's SyntaxError text. Regenerate with: python -m simulation.gen_scorecards_spec

cases.name: points-method-omitted-defaults-to-points
cases.note: scoring_method absent -> the else branch (points).

cases.name: points-method-unknown-falls-back-to-points
cases.note: An unrecognised scoring_method scores as points BUT is echoed verbatim in scoring_method.

cases.name: points-lower-boundary-inclusive
cases.note: min is inclusive.

cases.name: points-upper-boundary-inclusive
cases.note: max is inclusive (TS uses a half-open range).

cases.name: points-below-every-bin
cases.note: No range matches -> 0 points, active_range null.

cases.name: points-overlapping-ranges-first-wins
cases.note: Range scan breaks on the FIRST match, in list order — not the narrowest.

cases.name: points-missing-variable-defaults-to-zero
cases.note: A MISSING variable becomes 0 and can therefore MATCH a bin containing 0 and earn points.

cases.name: points-missing-variable-no-zero-bin
cases.note: Missing -> 0, which matches nothing here.

cases.name: points-null-value-matches-nothing
cases.note: An explicit null is NOT the missing-variable default: float(None) raises, so no range matches and the raw null is kept in the breakdown. Kotlin/Dart coerce null to 0.0 and would match [0,10] here — a real divergence.

cases.name: points-non-numeric-string-matches-nothing
cases.note: float('abc') raises -> no range matches, raw string kept. Kotlin/Dart coerce to 0.0 and match.

cases.name: points-numeric-string-matches
cases.note: Numeric strings are coerced by float().

cases.name: points-bool-true-is-one
cases.note: float(True) == 1.0.

cases.name: points-range-without-min-or-max
cases.note: A range with NO min/max defaults BOTH to 0 — it matches only the value 0. Kotlin/Dart substitute -inf/+inf for a null bound, so it matches everything there.

cases.name: points-range-with-null-min
cases.note: float(None) raises inside the scan -> the range is SKIPPED, not treated as open-ended.

cases.name: points-float-points-truncated
cases.note: int() truncates toward zero: 7.9 -> 7.

cases.name: points-negative-float-points-truncated
cases.note: -7.9 -> -7, toward zero.

cases.name: points-factor-without-variable-id
cases.note: variable_id absent -> lookup key None -> value defaults to 0 and matches [0,10].

cases.name: points-empty-bins
cases.note: Empty factor list: score is base_score, breakdown empty.

cases.name: points-clamped-to-max-score
cases.note: score = clamp(base + total, 0, max_score).

cases.name: points-clamped-to-zero
cases.note: The lower clamp is 0, NOT base_score.

cases.name: points-base-score-float-truncated
cases.note: int() on base_score/max_score truncates.

cases.name: points-base-score-defaults
cases.note: base_score defaults to 300 and max_score to 900.

cases.name: points-with-variable-lookup
cases.note: variable_lookup fills variable_name/source_id; without it both fall back to the id / null.

cases.name: weighted-half-truncates
cases.note: weighted_points = int(points * weight): 1.5 -> 1. TRUNCATION, not rounding.

cases.name: weighted-half-negative-truncates-toward-zero
cases.note: -1.5 -> -1 (toward zero), NOT -2. floor() would give -2.

cases.name: weighted-zero
cases.note: points is still recorded; only weighted_points is zeroed.

cases.name: weighted-negative-fractional-truncates-toward-zero
cases.note: int(7 * -0.5) = int(-3.5) = -3, not -4. Math.floor gives -4.

cases.name: weighted-negative-weight-negative-points
cases.note: int(-5 * -1.5) = int(7.5) = 7. Two negatives, so the sign flips back.

cases.name: weighted-negative-drives-score-below-zero
cases.note: 100 - 400 clamps at 0, the LOWER bound. Only max_score clamping was ported.

cases.name: weighted-per-factor-truncation-not-sum-then-truncate
cases.note: Each factor is truncated INDEPENDENTLY: 3*int(1.5) = 3, not int(3*1.5) = 4. An engine that sums in floating point and rounds once at the end gets a different score.

cases.name: woe-single-factor
cases.note: score = round(offset + (pdo/ln2) * (intercept + sum(coef*woe))), offset = target_score - (pdo/ln2)*ln(target_odds).

cases.name: woe-defaults-for-every-parameter
cases.note: intercept 0, pdo 20, target_score 600, target_odds 50 — an empty WoE card still scores 487.

cases.name: woe-no-range-matches-omits-woe-keys
cases.note: woe_details and information_value are ONLY present when at least one WoE range matched. A woe scorecard can therefore return NEITHER key.

cases.name: woe-partial-match
cases.note: Unmatched factors contribute woe 0.0 and are absent from woe_details, but STILL appear in breakdown.

cases.name: woe-boundary-max-inclusive-first-wins
cases.note: WoE bounds are CLOSED on both ends (min <= v <= max) and the first match wins, so v == 10 takes the FIRST bin. TypeScript uses >= min && < max and takes the second.

cases.name: woe-missing-iv-key-defaults-zero
cases.note: iv absent -> 0.0, but information_value is still emitted (as 0.0).

cases.name: woe-iv-accumulates-across-factors
cases.note: information_value is the SUM of matched-range iv over all factors.

cases.name: woe-missing-coefficient-defaults-zero
cases.note: coefficient absent -> 0.0, so a matched WoE contributes NOTHING to the score, yet still appears in woe_details and still adds its iv.

cases.name: woe-pdo-zero-uses-factor-one
cases.note: pdo <= 0 -> the scaling factor becomes 1, NOT pdo/ln(2). TS always divides.

cases.name: woe-target-odds-zero-drops-log-term
cases.note: target_odds <= 0 -> offset = target_score, the ln(target_odds) term is dropped entirely. TS computes Math.log(0) = -Infinity here.

cases.name: woe-string-parameters
cases.note: float() coerces string parameters.

cases.name: woe-rounding-half-down-to-even-0p5
cases.note: Python's round() is BANKER'S rounding (half to EVEN). Kotlin roundToInt() is half-up and Dart num.round() is half-away-from-zero; all three disagree on an exact .5.

cases.name: woe-rounding-half-up-to-even-1p5
cases.note: Python's round() is BANKER'S rounding (half to EVEN). Kotlin roundToInt() is half-up and Dart num.round() is half-away-from-zero; all three disagree on an exact .5.

cases.name: woe-rounding-half-down-to-even-again-2p5
cases.note: Python's round() is BANKER'S rounding (half to EVEN). Kotlin roundToInt() is half-up and Dart num.round() is half-away-from-zero; all three disagree on an exact .5.

cases.name: woe-rounding-negative-half-to-even-neg0p5
cases.note: Python's round() is BANKER'S rounding (half to EVEN). Kotlin roundToInt() is half-up and Dart num.round() is half-away-from-zero; all three disagree on an exact .5.

cases.name: woe-rounding-negative-half-away-neg1p5
cases.note: Python's round() is BANKER'S rounding (half to EVEN). Kotlin roundToInt() is half-up and Dart num.round() is half-away-from-zero; all three disagree on an exact .5.

cases.name: woe-clamped-to-max-score
cases.note: The WoE path clamps to [0, max_score] too — max_score is not a points-only concept.

cases.name: woe-factor-also-has-points-ranges
cases.note: Points are still computed and recorded in the breakdown under the woe method — they just do not reach the score.

cases.name: woe-with-variable-lookup
cases.note: woe_details carries variable_name from the lookup.

cases.name: points-method-still-emits-woe-details
cases.note: The WoE scan runs for EVERY scoring_method, so a POINTS scorecard that carries woe_values returns woe_details and information_value alongside a points score.

cases.name: formula-omitted-uses-default
cases.note: formula absent -> the default 'base_score + total_points'.

cases.name: formula-uses-total-woe-score
cases.note: total_woe_score IS in the formula context.

cases.name: formula-uses-variable-id-as-name
cases.note: Every breakdown entry's variable_id is bound to its RAW value in the formula scope.

cases.name: formula-excel-sum-list
cases.note: List literals are allowed so Excel aggregates can be called.

cases.name: formula-boolean-result-is-one
cases.note: isinstance(True, int) is True in Python, so a boolean formula scores 1 (or 0) — it does NOT fall back to base_score.

cases.name: formula-unknown-name-falls-back-to-base-score
cases.note: A FormulaError yields {'error': ...}, which is not int/float, so score = clamp(base_score).

cases.name: formula-string-result-falls-back
cases.note: A non-numeric result falls back to base_score.

cases.name: formula-score-name-not-in-context
cases.note: `score` is NOT in the formula context (it is being computed) — only the METRIC context has it.

cases.name: formula-total-iv-not-in-context
cases.note: `total_iv` is NOT in the formula context either, though it IS in the metric context. The two contexts are deliberately different.

cases.name: formula-attribute-access-rejected
cases.note: safe_formula (the allowlisting AST evaluator that replaced eval) refuses attribute access.

cases.name: formula-subscript-rejected
cases.note: `variables` IS bound in the context, but safe_formula allows no Subscript node, so indexing it is refused and the score falls back to base_score. This is a BEHAVIOUR CHANGE from the old eval()-based evaluator, where variables['a'] worked.

cases.name: formula-division-by-zero-falls-back-to-base
cases.note: ZeroDivisionError -> base_score, not 0 and not a raise.

cases.name: formula-syntax-error-falls-back-to-base
cases.note: unparseable -> base_score.

cases.name: formula-undefined-name-falls-back-to-base
cases.note: unbound name -> base_score.

cases.name: formula-negative-result-clamps-to-zero
cases.note: the LOWER clamp, which several ports omitted entirely.

cases.name: metrics-defaults
cases.note: name defaults to 'unnamed', formula to '0', unit to '' and category to 'financial'.

cases.name: metrics-duplicate-name-last-wins
cases.note: metrics is a dict keyed by name, so a duplicate name silently overwrites.

cases.name: metrics-empty-list-omits-key
cases.note: An empty metrics list means NO metrics key in the result at all.

cases.name: metrics-uses-score
cases.note: The metric context DOES bind `score` (the already-computed one).

cases.name: metrics-uses-total-iv
cases.note: The metric context also binds total_iv, which the formula context does not.

cases.name: metrics-error-value
cases.note: A failing metric does NOT abort the scorecard: its value becomes an error object and the sibling metrics still resolve.

cases.name: metrics-on-woe-scorecard
cases.note: Metrics run for every scoring method, over the already-clamped score.

cases.name: metrics-string-value
cases.note: A metric value is whatever the formula returns — it is not coerced to a number.

contract: score: exact integer match, required of every engine.
scoringMethod: echoed verbatim from the input, including unrecognised values.
breakdown[].weightedPoints: int(points * weight) — truncated PER FACTOR, never summed first.
Range/WoE bounds are closed on both ends (min <= v <= max) and the FIRST match wins.
A bound that is absent defaults to 0; a bound that is null (or any non-numeric) SKIPS the range.
A missing variable becomes 0; an explicit null or a non-numeric string matches no range at all.

woe score = clamp(round(offset + factor * (intercept + sum(coef*woe))), 0, max_score), factor = pdo/ln(2) when pdo > 0 else 1, offset = target_score - factor*ln(target_odds) when target_odds > 0 else target_score. round() is banker's rounding (half to even).
formula score = clamp(int(result), 0, max_score); a non-numeric result falls back to base_score. bool IS numeric here (int(True) == 1).
woe_details/information_value appear whenever ANY WoE range matched — for EVERY scoring method, not only 'woe' — and are absent entirely when none matched.
metrics appear only when the metrics list is non-empty; the metric context binds score and total_iv, the formula context binds neither.
